title: Trunk flexor EMG (raw) vs barbell height at constant L5-S1 moment (13.2 / 26.5 Nm)
subcategory: upright static load holding, co-contraction vs load height (stability)

quantity.name: raw EMG amplitude (not normalised)
quantity.definition: mean integrated EMG (30-250 Hz band-pass, rectified, 5 Hz Hanning low-pass) over middle 3 s of 5-s static holds; NOT normalised to MVC (authors note raw EMG); averaged across muscles of the composite; mean ± error bar (assumed SD, not stated) across 20 subjects

protocol.summary: Upright standing, normal lordosis maintained via electrogoniometer (T10-S1) feedback; subject held a barbell between two vertical guide bars at 30 cm horizontal from L5-S1 and heights 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 cm above the sacrum, with 4.5 or 9.0 kg (external moment 13.2 / 26.5 Nm constant over heights); 2 trials per condition.
how_to_simulate: Upright neutral posture (lordosis as in relaxed standing)
Place 4.5 kg or 9.0 kg (both hands) 30 cm anterior to L5-S1 at 0-80 cm above the sacrum (arm posture changes with height)
Compare RELATIVE change of predicted flexor activation vs the 0-cm condition (raw EMG in mV cannot be compared in absolute terms); flexor co-activation should rise with height, more at 26.5 Nm
Stability-based models: check whether antagonist (abdominal) activation increases with load height at constant moment
protocol.notes: EMG not normalised, so only within-study ratios/trends are meaningful. Females recruited 32% more flexor co-activation than males (text); gender x height interaction significant (p<0.001), difference significant only at 60 and 80 cm. Error bars in Fig 4 are presumably SD (caption silent).

extraction.uncertainty: flexor ±0.3 mV, extensor ±0.6 mV (bar tops, 300 dpi; axis calibrated on ticks); error bars ±0.5/±1 mV
extraction.check_notes: Pixel-detected bar tops/whiskers re-read visually: flexor 13.2 Nm @0 cm ≈8.1 (bar) /10.5 (whisker); flexor 26.5 Nm @80 cm ≈25.9/40.5; extensor 26.5 Nm @60 cm ≈66/97.5 - agree.

pass_rule.rule: trend: model activation ratio (h/h0) within the measured ratio ± SD/mean; increase with height and with load reproduced
